title: Variables corrupted after setting device name
user_question: threshold should be 512 but prints a random number.

reference_context.title: Arduino Language Reference (arduino.cc)
reference_context.document: Arduino Language Reference: array / string (char array)
reference_context.revision: arduino/reference-en master, last commit b367b025a1 (2025-04-11); rendered at docs.arduino.cc/language-reference
reference_context.section: Variables > Data Types > array (Accessing an Array); string (Null termination)
reference_context.snippet: Writing to random memory locations is definitely a bad idea and can often lead to unhappy results such as crashes or program malfunction. [...] Unlike BASIC or JAVA, the C++ compiler does no checking to see if array access is within legal bounds of the array size that you have declared. [string:] This means that your string needs to have space for one more character than the text you want it to contain.

expected.root_cause: strcpy writes an 18-character string (19 bytes with terminator) into an 8-byte buffer, overflowing into the next struct member, threshold (bytes 's','e' = 0x6573 = 25971).
expected.fix: Enlarge deviceName (at least 19 bytes) or use strncpy/strlcpy with sizeof(deviceName).
